name: Malta
tagline: An English-speaking EU island that treats the IB as its own
ownCitizens: If you hold Maltese citizenship, the parts of this page written for other EU/EEA citizens — registering your right of residence, proving your fee status — are not about you, and Malta's own student grants and loans are open to you on their ordinary terms; check them, because some depend on where you have lived. Your IB is still a foreign qualification here, so the IB entry rules on this page still apply to you.
summary: Malta is an EU country where university teaching is in English, and the University of Malta handles the IB as a local qualification with a published entry rule: the Diploma with 28 points. EU students pay no tuition there. You apply directly to each institution; the year starts in October, which leaves room after IB results in July.
whyConsider: Teaching in English, inside the EU.
No tuition for EU/EEA students at the University of Malta or MCAST.
A clear published IB rule at the University of Malta: 28 points, with passes in a language, a science and a humanistic subject.
The academic year starts on 4 October 2027, three months after IB results.
watchOuts: The University of Malta had not published its 2027 deadlines on 24 September 2026. Applications normally open in November.
Choose "Local Qualifications" for the IB on the University of Malta application. It is easy to get wrong.
The general requirement includes SEC Maltese. If you were educated abroad you may offer another language instead (not English), with Admissions Board approval.
Medicine is different: you must pass a Medical Maltese exam, and in 2026 IB applicants had to apply by 16 March.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: University of Malta: the IB Diploma with at least 28 points, and passes at 3 or better in a language, a science and a humanistic subject.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: HL normally counts where a MATSEC Advanced Level is required, SL where an Intermediate Level is required. IB 7 to 3 correspond to MATSEC A to E.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The University of Malta teaches in English.
language.englishProof: IB English A (HL or SL) or English B HL at 4 or more exempts you from the University of Malta's English test. Otherwise present a test such as IELTS 6.0 by 30 September.

feeContext.summary: No tuition at the University of Malta for a bachelor's ('No fees apply', on its bachelor's pages), nor at MCAST. The UM application fee is EUR 35 with the IB.
Set per course at the University of Malta: EUR 8,500 to EUR 26,000 a year on the four 2026-27 courses read (the M.D. is EUR 26,000).

sectorLandscape.summary: Three public institutions accredit their own degrees: the University of Malta, MCAST and the Institute of Tourism Studies. Alongside them are private institutions licensed by the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA).

routes.what: The national university. Bachelor’s to doctorate, taught in English. Takes the IB directly as a local qualification.

routes.englishName: Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology
routes.what: The public college of arts, science and technology, which accredits its own programmes up to master’s level (MQF 7) and offers undergraduate degrees.
routes.note: Teaches in English and is free for EU students. Applies through its own portal. IB entry rules are not covered here.

routes.what: The public institute for tourism, hospitality and culinary arts, accrediting its own programmes.
routes.note: Three bachelor's degrees, taught in English, on its Luqa campus. IB entry rules are not covered here.

routes.what: Licensed private providers such as the American University of Malta, St Martin's Institute and Global College Malta. Each sets its own admissions and fees.
routes.note: The regulator, MFHEA (mfhea.mt), publishes the list of licensed institutions.

notes: Tuition checked on four University of Malta 2026-7 course pages (EU: no fees; non-EU EUR 8,500-26,000), not the whole catalogue. The 2027-8 course pages were not yet published on 24 September 2026.
Not established: the 2027 deadlines, and whether the Admissions Board approves another language in place of Maltese as a matter of course.
